subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a rich 3D model, keeping it compact but detailed, with wheels sized so their lowest point touches y=0, importing from the builder library and its glow kit.

My design concept is a cyberpunk militarized pickup: angular armored wedge cab, hexagonal run-flat wheels, neon strips, roof turret with railgun, rocket pods, light bar, rear thrusters, cargo bed with side skirts, and SVG decals like hazard stripes, an emblem, numbering, and glowing screens and headlights.

For the skeleton I'm keeping it moderate -- chassis root, steerable front wheel joints, spinning wheels, turret yaw/pitch, and maybe a hatch or fan, skipping doors to save complexity. For colors I'm going with a gunmetal paint with countershading rather than toon shading, using a limited flat color palette, and I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and a shortcut part-placement function before writing the actual model code.

Now I'm working out the vehicle's dimensions and wheel placement, then planning the body construction using extruded profile shapes -- a wedge-like silhouette for the main hull and a narrower extruded cab greenhouse with a separate glass layer for the windows.

Defining the hull profile coordinates...

Still shaping cab geometry...

Now I'm working out the hood's sloped surface to position scoop and vent details along it, then shifting to the truck bed: a floor box plus side walls and a tailgate positioned behind the cab.

For cargo, I'm planning a hex container, a battery/generator unit, missile rack, roof-mounted twin-barrel railgun turret, bed-mounted rocket pods, ammo crates, and a radar dish, then starting on rear thruster bells.

Now I'm designing each wheel corner: tire cylinder with tread blocks, hex rim with a neon glow ring, bolted hub, armor disc cover, and fender arches built as extruded shapes with a hole cut for the wheel.

Working out the fender flare arc geometry...

Adjusting hull thickness to 1.7 and repositioning wheels to x±1.0 so the fender flares and arches clear properly, bringing total width to about 2.32. I'm also sketching side skirt panels between the wheels with angled plates and considering a hazard-stripe paint texture for them.

Now I'm planning out the various decal textures: hazard stripe cards near the bumper, a door emblem, a tailgate number plate reading "MK-77 // 2077", screen UI textures for the dash and side display, a cargo crate label, and door graphics using shapes rather than risky custom fonts.

For the hull paint, I'm designing a digital camo pattern using hex-cell noise with a few dark cyber tones and panel seam overlays. Then I'm working out texture placement—mapping decal planes onto the flat hull sides, handling mirroring so the left and right sides read correctly, and figuring out how the plane's axis orientation affects texture direction.

Checking the orientation math, I verify that for both the left and right hull sides the local coordinate derivation gives the correct reading direction from a viewer's perspective, confirming the mirrored texture logic works on either side.

Now I'm planning the turret details: yaw and pitch joints at the roof, a railgun with twin rails and a glowing capacitor gap, plus roof-mounted light bar, antenna whip with dish, and sensor dome. For the rocket pods, I'm working out the rotation math so the angled tubes tip correctly upward rather than down when placed on the bed walls.

I'm setting up helper functions to place parts using quaternions, mapping local pod geometry into model coordinates so each piece orients correctly along the frame. I'm also picking the neon palette—cyan and magenta accents with amber lighting—for glow strips running under the vehicle's skirts.

Now I'm detailing the cab: roof panels, vents, door seams, glowing handle strips, mirror cameras, a spinning rooftop sensor array, and slatted bar armor across the windshield. I'm also planning the bed with a cargo container, generator cylinders, and labeled ammo crates, plus front-end details like a wedge bumper, winch plate, tow hooks, and glowing headlight slits.

I'm sketching a rear rotating radar dish and glowing battery pack for the bed, targeting a part count around 250-300 with a compact but rich codebase. I'm defining the camo paint pattern with mixed dark panel colors, lightened highlights, and bottom grime, then building a paneled hull material using rivets and aspect ratio settings.

I'm figuring out which builder imports I need, pulling in paint utilities like mix, noise, cells, and gradient, plus the panelled helper from the clockwork kit, and adding metal finishes for parts like the barrel. Now I'm settling on a flat color palette with dark steel, cyan, magenta, amber, and a tinted dark glass tone.

Setting up imports and color constants...

I'm designing the plate with "NX-2077" text in bold monospace, then working out where to place a small CRT-style screen with cyan bars and a radar display, settling on the rear cab panel above the bed facing outward.

Now I'm planning a crate label with hazard stripes and "AMMO" text with a warning triangle, and thinking through headlight glow and grille detailing. Setting up small geometry helper functions for boxes and cylinders...

Setting up joints for the chassis and wheel assemblies...

Still designing the wheel assembly...

Placing the brake caliper on the steer/mount bone instead, with wheel centers positioned along the x-axis and hub height set. For suspension I'm keeping it simple — control arm rods from chassis to hub, stacked torus coil springs, and a glowing shock rod, all attached to the rigid chassis bone. Now moving on to extruding the hull outline for the main body.

The bumper wedge extends out to the hull front, so I'm planning a front bumper with painted armor color, plus plow teeth spikes along the lower edge, tow hooks, and a light bar mounted near the headlights at the hull's front face.

I'm placing the grille between the headlights with glowing magenta bars, then working on the hood geometry—calculating its sloped surface profile and adding glowing vent slots angled to match the hood's forward tilt.

Now adding a central hood scoop with a glowing intake slit, plus ERA brick arrays along the hood sides, and starting on the cab's side windows shaped to follow the windshield's slanted front edge.

Adding armored window slats and frame bars across the side windows and windshield, then starting on a roof plate above the cabin.

Now I'm planning the roof details—hatch lid, sensor cluster, antennas, light bar—and designing the turret: a yaw joint at the rear roof pivoting vertically, a pitch joint above it for tilting the gun, with drum base, cheek armor plates, sensor box, and trunnion rod to connect them.

I'm roughing out the railgun barrel assembly—paired rods with a glowing gap between them, coil rings, heat fins, and a muzzle brake—then checking overall turret height stays reasonable around 2.7m.

Now I'm laying out the truck bed: floor panel with ribbing, and side walls positioned along the bed's length and height.

For the wheel wells I'm figuring out how to avoid the rear wheels poking through the bed walls—adjusting wall height and adding a lower skirt panel so fenders can cover the overlap cleanly.

Overlapping is acceptable here, so I'll move on to planning the bed contents: glowing cylindrical battery cells in a frame, textured ammo crates, a rotating radar dish at the rear, and tilted rocket pods mounted on top of the side walls.

Adding more structure elements...

Working out the skirt profile shape, adding a glowing cyan accent rod beneath it, and placing a door emblem decal on the hull side between the wheel arches.

Now I'm adding door seam details using thin frame boxes, a small glowing magenta handle, and planning fender flare arcs over each wheel using the armor material.

For sensors, I'm designing a roof-mounted glass dome, a spinning lidar ring with a glowing slit, whip antennas with spiked tips, a small dish, and a light bar on the roof with alternating amber, magenta, and cyan glow segments. I'm also placing camera-style mirrors on stalks beside the cab, and planning the underbody with a driveshaft, differential, glowing underglow strips, and an exhaust system.

I'm switching the exhaust to vertical ringed stacks mounted behind the cab with glowing tips, adding a rear holo-screen frame with a glowing texture plane, and sketching roof side rails plus sagging cable bundles swept between the turret base and hull. I'm skipping the plate number and hover features, and now moving on to how the front wheels mount.

Front bumper fog lights get an amber glow instead of red, and I'm settling on iron/steel metal paints for armor since flat emitter colors stay within the color budget. Writing pod helper code...

I'm placing the railgun relative to the pitch bone in model space, then adding a hazard decal plane on the bumper's front face with a texture sized to fit that panel.

Working out the rear bumper hazard orientation and the tailgate plate decal placement, figuring out correct texture axes for each facing direction. I'll skip the windshield banner and hood decals, moving on to the door emblem plane instead.

I'm adding magenta underglow rods beneath the hull near the center, distinct from the cyan skirt lighting. Tallying up the part count across wheels, suspension, and body pieces to stay comfortably under the 1000-part budget, and counting textures used so far before considering one more vent grille decal.

Deciding to add a sixth texture: a bold "07" numeral decal with an outline on the rear bed wall, sized and positioned on the flank. Now writing the final export, being careful to use number arrays for positions and keep TypeScript strictness reasonable.

Still writing builder code...

Still defining wheel joints...

Still placing wheel details...

Now I'm adding the brake disc and caliper near the rim, mounted on a suspension bone, before starting on the A-arm suspension rods from the chassis.

For the suspension, I'm stacking small rotated tori to form a coil spring between the arm and hub, plus a glowing magenta shock rod through the center, checking that they stay tucked beneath the hull's visible gap.

Now I'm repositioning the suspension lower, around y .4, with an axle tube spanning the wheel width plus a differential pumpkin sphere, so the A-arms and shocks peek out visibly between the wheel and hull.

I'm skipping separate springs and instead pairing simple shock rods angled near each wheel, then adding driveshafts, A-arm rods, and a steering link for enough visual detail without overcomplicating things. Moving to the underbody, I'm placing a battery/fuel tank box centered beneath the chassis.

For paint logic, I'm writing a camo shader using cell-based noise to assign each patch a color from a dark tactical palette.

Defining the material palettes now (hull camo, bump metal, steel, gun-blued) and starting to lay out roof plate geometry with its box dimensions and position.

I'm working through placement conflicts for the roof details -- turret ring, hatch lid with hinge and coaming, light bar, sensor dome, and spinning LIDAR -- adjusting their x/z coordinates so they don't overlap each other.

Now I'm positioning the turret assembly itself: the ring torus and drum cylinder for yaw rotation, side cheek boxes, and the pitch pivot with trunnion rod for the barrel, making sure the gun barrel clears the light bar as it points forward.

Adding more weapon details...

I'm positioning the stacked crates so they don't collide with the radar, splitting them to the right side at a couple of z-depths with a smaller rotated one on top, while keeping the battery and radar on the left side at separate z positions to avoid overlap.

I'm placing the tailgate joint at the rear of the bed and defining the hull-to-bed boundary along z, then adding a rear bumper. For detailing I'm adding glowing cyan trim rods along the bed wall tops and magenta skirt rods along the hull's lower edge, plus a secondary thin glowing ring around the fender arcs just outside the main flare.

Now I'm sizing the fender flares and figuring out the arc placement for the neon rim trim, then setting up headlight and taillight glow colors (cyan-white with magenta DRL accents up front, red in back) and adding thin dark seam boxes to suggest cab door lines.

I'm placing door emblems, roof hatch details, and side vents, then building forward-facing bumper spikes in a ring pattern. I'm also sketching tow hooks, a winch drum with glowing fairlead, and amber fog lights at the bumper corners.

Now I'm adding a front sensor grill with glowing magenta rods along the slanted hood face, backed by a dark box for contrast, and double-checking color consistency before finalizing the root return and verifying the wheels sit flush on the floor.

Writing pod placement logic...

Adding missile pod details with cylinder mounts and spike-nosed missiles oriented by quaternion, plus side mount arms connecting to the wall. Keeping the whole thing around 450 lines before finalizing.
